description: The plot illustrates the performance on Qwen2.5, comparing accuracy across different co-occurrence numbers for six methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale for values above zero, with visible tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and features a linear scale ranging from 60 to 85, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 5. All six methods are represented by solid lines that exhibit a steady upward trend across the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, starting at an accuracy of approximately 64% and rising to about 71% at the end of the x-axis. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning near 65% and increasing to roughly 73%. The "IKE" method uses a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at approximately 67% and ending near 75%. The "MEND" method is depicted by a brown line with diamond markers, which starts around 69% and climbs to approximately 80%. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, beginning near 70% and rising to about 77%. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 74% and reaching roughly 84% at the end of the x-axis.
